Thanks for the sample and the patience while we pulled the runbook together. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to immediately and what will be part of the migration carve-out path:

What we can commit to (contract language we propose):
- Regional p50/p95 numeric targets (example table below). These will be included as a regional appendix to the SLO section.
- Measurement: contractual p95 will be computed over 1h epochs, using our standard aggregation (weighted by token count for generation endpoints). Operational alerting uses a 5m rolling window.

Ephemeral-offset policy (temporary derating):
- Automatic carve-out: bursts under 2 minutes where instantaneous RPS >= 8x baseline and where our edge shows prefix- cache-miss ratio > 50%. Customer must upload the traffic sample and request ids within 48 hours.
- Manual derating: for migration windows longer than 2 minutes but under 6 hours, customer can request a temporary derating. Required evidence: (1) request sample csv, (2) representative error/trace ids, (3) start/end timestamps, (4) business-impact statement. Requests evaluated within 4 business hours; derating if approved is limited to specific routes and will include a rollback criterion.

Attachments sent: proposed-window-evidence.pdf (checklist) and a short template for a regional appendix.
